project.title: Conspiracy Bench
project.summary: A benchmark that tests whether language models stick to the documented facts on topics that attract conspiracy theories.

overview.researchQuestion: How hard is it to teach a model something that it should not know?
overview.motivation: Conspiracy theories are already in models' pre-training data, but a model shouldn't believe them. More dangerous knowledge, like biorisk data, is in the same position. That makes conspiracy theories a safe way to test how teachable models are and how far pressure can push them.

phases.title: Phase 1 · Build the benchmark
phases.description: Write question-and-answer pairs that test whether a model believes a conspiracy theory. A judge scores each answer as hold, diverge or abstain, including under scripted pushback.

phases.title: Phase 2 · Hill-climb it
phases.description: Benchmark a model, then fine-tune it together to believe these claims and measure how much that takes.

notes: Compute is provided. Contributors submit experiment proposals.
Questions are global, not limited to Western conspiracy theories.
